ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (No 35 of 2009), as amended, particularly Part 1 sections 10-18 (customer due diligence), sections 31-34 (beneficial ownership and control), and section 81 (PEP screening); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; Companies Act 1993 (No 105 of 1993), sections 87-90 (share register and ownership records); Privacy Act 2020; and the AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011 (SR 2011/224). There is no separate public UBO register decree in New Zealand; beneficial ownership data is collected internally by reporting entities and is subject to lawful inspection by the Financial Intelligence Unit, Inland Revenue Department, and Companies Office.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: obtain certified copy from the Companies Office, have a New Zealand notary public attest the copy, then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) attaches an Apostille certificate. Consular legalization is not used for Hague Convention states; for a non-Hague destination, MFAT certification is followed by consular legalization at the destination embassy. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille only: request the certificate from the Companies Office, notarise the certificate, and obtain an MFAT Apostille. If the destination country is not a party to the Apostille Convention, use MFAT authentication plus destination consulate legalization. The two authentication systems are parallel, mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution approving incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the beneficial owner / incorporating parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a New Zealand notary public of the resolution signature page, thereafter MFAT Apostille for Hague Convention states. For non-member states, the MFAT Legalization Section certifies the notarized resolution and the destination consulate performs consular legalization; do not chain the Apostille and consular steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitution of the New Zealand company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator and initial shareholders executing the company Constitution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: the fully executed Constitution is notarially certified, then MFAT issues a Hague Apostille. Non-Hague states require MFAT certification followed by consular legalization at the destination mission; select the route opposite to the destination's treaty status, never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter including UBO confirmation and transaction profile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand registered commercial bank (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac NZ) after completion of customer due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank reference letter notarised, then MFAT Apostille. If the receiving jurisdiction is not party to the Apostille Convention, present the notarised letter to MFAT for authentication and then to the relevant embassy/consulate for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, UBOs, authorised signatories, and material counterparties against: the UN Security Council Consolidated List; OFAC SDN and 51% ownership rules; New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit domestic sanctions and persons of interest lists; UK HM Treasury Consolidated List; and global PEP databases such as World-Check/Refinitiv or Dow Jones. At the Medium_Risk_Enhanced banking level, screening must occur at onboarding and be repeated daily, with ongoing transaction monitoring and at least annual re-screening. Any positive PEP, sanctions, or adverse media match requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and a Suspicious Transaction Report to the NZ FIU if not conclusively deconflicted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Services: Company Name Search and Reservation Portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) using the 'Search the Register' and 'Reserve a Name' functions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin alphabet characters (A-Z) and Arabic numerals 0-9; hyphens, ampersands, and parentheses are permitted within defined positions. Maori macronized vowels are registrable but should be transliterated into unaccented Latin characters for IRD and banking systems that do not support diacritics. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) legal element, being the mandatory suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd'; (2) distinctive unique element, being the invented or natural-person identifier; (3) descriptive business element such as 'Ventilator Manufacturing'; and (4) restricted or sensitive element requiring prior ministerial approval. The name must be distinguishable from existing names and must not be misleading under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant has 15 working days from the date of the Registrar's notice to file a formal reconsideration request with the Registrar of Companies at the Companies Office, MBIE. The request must include the proposed name, the original application reference, detailed reasons why the name is not prohibited, evidence of prior use, trademark registration or goodwill, and any ministerial consent obtained. The Registrar must issue a final written decision. If refused, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972 within 28 days. For reservation expiry, a new name reservation application must be submitted; extension is not automatic but may be sought in exceptional circumstances by emailing the Companies Office with a supporting statutory declaration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office providing a genuine physical New Zealand street address and regular document collection is permissible as a registered office under the Companies Act 1993, provided it is not a PO Box and is open during normal business hours. However, the Inland Revenue Department and all New Zealand trading banks reject a virtual-office-only arrangement for an active manufacturing company in the medical device sector because there is no demonstrable local premises, payroll, fixed assets, or operational substance. For ISIC 3250 ICU ventilator manufacturing, MEDSAFE requires an actual manufacturing and quality control facility plus an ISO 13485 quality management system; therefore a virtual office can only serve as an ancillary administrative seat, never as the commercial substance center of the entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspections by IRD, the Companies Office, or local councils are triggered by red flags such as a 100% virtual office, no factory assets, and inconsistent import/export data. Quantified risk: 15-20% if a real manufacturing facility exists and is staffed; 70-80% if the company relies solely on a virtual office. Physical inspection checklist: (a) business licence and occupational safety signage; (b) ventilator assembly line, test benches, and ISO 13485 documentation; (c) raw material inventory and supplier invoices; (d) employee records, PAYE, and timesheets; (e) bank statements and GST filings; (f) board meeting minutes and statutory records. Failure to produce any item constitutes a red flag and may lead to de-registration or AML/CFT licence suspension proceedings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), Part 2 (Incorporation), including sections 10, 12, 13, 16, 19, 40, 44, 126, 185, 189 and 407; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2014; and the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Limited Company (New Zealand Companies Office electronic filing), together with consents and constitution if adopted.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 1993 for an NZ_LTD. The company must allot at least one ordinary share, and each subscriber may satisfy the subscription price in cash, property, or enforceable promise. There is no blocked escrow account requirement; however, paid-up subscription proceeds must be received in cleared funds and recorded in the share register, and bank AML/CFT rules require source-of-funds evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION IN WRITING OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF NZ_LTD, ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE DIRECTORS PURSUANT TO SECTION 407 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 (NEW ZEALAND)

WHEREAS the Company was incorporated on [date] under the Companies Act 1993 with the name NZ_LTD and with a New Zealand Business Number; and WHEREAS the initial subscribers have agreed to subscribe for ordinary shares and to provide working capital for the registered undertaking, namely the manufacture and assembly of turbine-driven invasive critical-care mechanical ventilators and related life-support hardware; and WHEREAS the directors must establish the registered office, banking facilities, share capital arrangements, statutory officers, and compliance functions of the Company;

NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company is established at [New Zealand street address]. The Board confirms that the office is a physical New Zealand street address, open and accessible during ordinary business hours, and suitable for service of legal process. The Board appoints [name] as the authorised service contact. Any change of registered office must be lodged with the Registrar within the statutory time frame.

2. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The Board approves the allotment of ordinary shares to the initial subscribers as recorded in the share register. Each subscriber shall pay the agreed subscription consideration in cleared funds into the Company's bank account. The Board confirms that no minimum paid-up capital is required by law and that no escrow condition applies. The directors are authorised to issue share certificates, maintain the shareholder register, and record any unpaid amounts as calls on shares.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board designates [Bank], [branch address], as the principal banker of the Company. The directors, jointly or severally, or such officers as the Board may nominate, are authorised to open all bank accounts, sign all account mandates, operate internet banking, issue and sign cheques, apply for Government letters of credit, arrange SWIFT wire facilities, and execute indemnities and financial security documents on behalf of the Company.

4. STATUTORY OFFICERS AND GOVERNANCE. The Board appoints [name] as Managing Director, [name] as Chief Financial Officer, and, if considered appropriate, [name] as Company Secretary with responsibility for filing statutory returns and maintaining corporate registers. All directors have signed their consents to act and satisfy the natural-person and disqualification requirements under the Companies Act 1993.

5. INDUSTRIAL AND LICENSING MANDATE. Management is directed to apply expeditiously for all building, environmental, fire safety, WorkSafe, and Medsafe authorisations required for the manufacture of medical ventilators and for the occupation and operation of the manufacturing and warehousing premises.

6. GENERAL. This resolution shall be entered into the minute book and is binding on all directors, officers, shareholders, and appointed agents. The Board authorises the Managing Director to execute all contracts and instruments necessary to implement this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Online Incorporation Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online portal, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Companies Office registration service and verify that the proposed name NZ_LTD includes Limited or Ltd and does not conflict with an existing company name or business identifier. Prepare and submit Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Limited Company together with each director's signed consent to act, each shareholder's consent, the registered office street address in New Zealand, address for service, and a constitution if the subscribers elect to adopt one. Pay the prescribed incorporation fee. After completion, the Companies Office will issue a certificate of incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number. All directors and shareholders must pass identity verification and provide their addresses subject to statutory privacy protections.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name with Limited or Ltd suffix
Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Limited Company
Signed consent to act as director for each director
Consent of each initial shareholder
Registered office street address in New Zealand
Address for service in New Zealand
Constitution (if adopted)
Passport and proof of residential address for each director and shareholder
Prescribed filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended due to name conflict, data mismatch, or identity verification failure, the applicant may revise the application and submit an alternative company name or corrected information through the same online portal. If a signed consent is defective, obtain a fresh wet-ink or verified digital consent. If the Registrar issues a compliance query, respond within 10 working days with the requested declarations, translations, or evidence of address; no new incorporation fee is imposed for correcting the same application unless a company name change is requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Allotment and Subscription Funding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board and New Zealand registered bank or licensed trust-account provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a board meeting or adopt a written resolution approving the allotment of ordinary shares to the initial subscribers. Execute share subscription letters and collect the consideration in cleared funds into the Company's bank account or a solicitor's trust account acting for the Company. Record each subscriber's name, shareholding percentage, payment amount, and payment date in the share register. The board must issue share certificates promptly and, if a subscriber defaults, record the unpaid call as a liability in the share register. The Company must simultaneously submit a business bank account application including beneficial ownership declarations, entity structure, actual or intended premises, and source-of-funds evidence for the paid-in capital.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Board resolution approving share allotment
Share subscription letters from each subscriber
Company share register in prescribed form
Sources of funds declaration and bank statements
AML/CFT KYC business questionnaire
List of beneficial owners, shareholders, and directors
Share certificate template for issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence because medical hardware manufacturing is treated as medium-risk, provide a group structure chart, proof of beneficial ownership, the ultimate human persons, source of wealth, and transaction flow. If a subscription payment is rejected or delayed, defer share certificate issuance until cleared funds are received and record a note in the share register. If the share structure changes, file any necessary notice with the Companies Office and maintain statutory records to avoid a compliance notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption and Statutory Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Nominate a physical New Zealand address for the registered office and identify an address for service. If the address has changed after incorporation, file the prescribed notice of change of registered office through the Companies Office digital portal. For officer appointments, ensure every director is at least 18 years old, is a natural person, is not subject to a statutory disqualification, and has executed a signed consent to act. The Board must appoint a Managing Director and a Chief Financial Officer by formal resolution and record the appointment in the company minutes. The Company must then file any director appointment or change with the Registrar within the required statutory time frame, ordinarily 15 working days, and verify that the Company's constitution permits the number of directors appointed.
required_dossiers: Form or notice of appointment/change of director
Registered office address confirmation and lease or utility proof
Address for service nomination
Directors' signed consents to act
Board minute appointing Managing Director and Chief Financial Officer
Director residential address and service address details
Companies Office online customer login authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the registered office address because it is a mailbox or virtual office, provide documentary proof of a physical occupied workspace. If a director consent is not witnessed or signed correctly, obtain a fresh signature or attach a statutory declaration. If a notification of appointment is filed late, submit an explanation and pay the applicable late filing fee; the appointment remains valid once the statutory form is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking Mandate and International Payment Rail Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand commercial bank trade finance desk and AML/CFT compliance unit.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the business banking and trade finance application to establish Government letter of credit and SWIFT wire payment rails. Submit a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, NZBN, board banking mandate, constituent documents, beneficial ownership declaration, and director identification. The bank will conduct a customer risk assessment based on the nature of life-support hardware manufacturing, target counterparties, and overseas payment jurisdictions. The board must pass a banking resolution specifying signatory thresholds for daily operations, authorised persons for letters of credit, and high-value transfer approvals. The facility documents should require the bank to verify all counterparties against applicable sanctions lists and provide settlement in agreed currencies.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation
Board resolution on bank signatories and facilities
Company constitution and Companies Office extract
Beneficial ownership declaration
Directors' passport and proof of residential address
Lease or physical premises proof for registered office
Trade finance credit application and LC facility form
SWIFT wire and banking mandate instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank places the facility under enhanced monitoring, execute the additional AML/CFT information request, provide bank reference letters, cash-flow projections, supplier and purchaser lists, and regulatory clearance evidence. If a signatory is rejected by the bank integrity check, replace that officer through a new board resolution and resubmit the mandate. If trade finance is unavailable at the first bank, approach a bank with established medical export finance capabilities and provide an independent compliance opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Premises, Environmental, Building, and Fire Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local territorial authority; regional council; WorkSafe New Zealand; Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the territorial authority for building occupancy approval and any required premises permit for the manufacture and warehousing of turbine-driven ICU ventilators. Determine with the regional council whether the assembly, testing, cleaning, painting, or controlled-environment processes trigger a resource consent for discharges to air, water, or land. Prepare an Assessment of Environmental Effects if a discretionary or restricted discretionary activity is proposed. Obtain a fire safety certificate from FENZ and, if any hazardous substances such as oxygen cylinders, solvent-based lubricants, battery packs, or epoxy resins are stored, an approved hazardous substances location. Apply to WorkSafe for an occupational health and safety clearance and for any electrical or pressure-equipment certification required by the proposed turbine and pneumatic test systems.
required_dossiers: Building occupancy application and fit-out plans
Resource consent application and Assessment of Environmental Effects
Site plan, floor layout, and proposed process flow
Hazardous substances inventory and safety data sheets
Wastewater and air emission estimates for manufacturing operations
Fire evacuation plan and emergency response procedures
Structural load calculations for cleanrooms, benches, and storage racks
Electrical test certificates and pressure equipment certificates
WorkSafe health and safety methodology statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the regional council requests further information, respond within the specified time frame, often 20 working days, and provide revised emissions modelling. If the territorial authority refuses a building permit, correct the drawing or fire safety deficiencies and resubmit. If FENZ issues a non-compliance notice, install required detection, suppression, separation, or emergency lighting and schedule a re-inspection before commencing production.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medsafe and WorkSafe Product Manufacturing Clearance for Medical Ventilators
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority (Medsafe); WorkSafe New Zealand; accredited conformity assessment body.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the invasive turbine-driven critical-care ventilator under the New Zealand medical device framework and prepare a technical dossier demonstrating compliance with applicable safety and performance standards, including ISO 80601-2-12 for critical-care ventilators, electrical safety, biocompatibility, usability, and software validation. Lodge the device conformity assessment and facility registration dossier with Medsafe, or with an authorised accredited assessor under Medsafe's recognised pathway, before supplying the device in New Zealand. This filing must describe the manufacturing environment, cleanroom controls, sterilisation or sanitisation procedures, production and process validation, quality management under ISO 13485, and post-market surveillance plan. In parallel, obtain WorkSafe approval for any occupational hazards created by assembly, pneumatic testing, ultrasonic welding, volatile adhesives, or high-pressure gas systems. No commercial production may begin until the premises, environmental, fire, and product-file clearances are issued.
required_dossiers: Medical device classification and intended purpose statement
ISO 13485 quality management system certificate or gap assessment
Technical file or design dossier for the ventilator
ISO 80601-2-12 performance and safety reports
Electrical safety and electromagnetic compatibility test reports
Biocompatibility and conformity statements
Software validation and cybersecurity documentation
Clinical evaluation and usability validation documents
Factory and process flow plan including cleanroom zones
Hazardous substances location approval and WorkSafe assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Medsafe or the accredited assessor issues deficiency findings, submit a corrective and preventive action plan, additional test reports, and revised labelling. If WorkSafe issues an improvement notice, halt any hazardous operation until safety methods are corrected. If the conformity assessment timeline exceeds the SLA because of clinical data requests, the company may apply for accelerated review only if a legitimate clinical emergency need is demonstrated; otherwise continue the file until all conditions are satisfied.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Medsafe (New Zealand Medicines and Medical Devices Safety Authority), WorkSafe New Zealand, New Zealand Fire and Emergency (FENZ), local territorial authority, and the applicable regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: New Zealand Medical Device Manufacturing Facility and Product Conformity Authorization; Resource Management Act 1991 Resource Consent; Building Warrant of Fitness; Fire and Emergency New Zealand Hazardous Substances and Fire Safety Location Approval; WorkSafe New Zealand Health and Safety Clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand in coordination with the relevant regional council and territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Full Assessment of Environmental Effects and Resource Consent required as a discretionary or restricted discretionary activity for manufacturing, assembly, cleaning, and warehousing operations that discharge contaminants to air or wastewater. A permitted activity exemption is not available for a ventilators-manufacturing facility handling solvents, sealants, lubricants, packaged gases, battery components, or process wastewaters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater quality before discharge or municipal sewer acceptance: pH 6.0-9.0; biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) not exceeding 20 mg/L; total suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L; no visible free oils, grease, or scum; and no objectionable odour beyond the site boundary. Ambient air: fine particulate matter PM10 24-hour mean must not exceed 50 µg/m3; volatile organic compound emissions and airborne particulates from soldering, solvent cleaning, adhesives, painting, and turbine assembly must be controlled by extraction, filtration, and best available technique standards. Hazardous waste, including spent solvents, epoxy compounds, contaminated wipes, and aerosol canisters, must be segregated, covered, stored in impermeable secondary containment, and transported only by an authorised hazardous waste carrier.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defence and fire clearance requires a first fire safety certificate and annual building warrant of fitness from the territorial authority, structural load inspection for cleanroom platforms, storage racks, and turbine support frames, and hazardous-substances location approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand for oxygen, compressed gases, volatile cleaners, and lithium batteries. Occupational clearance requires WorkSafe New Zealand approval of the assembly and enclosed-equipment protocols, electrical safety certification, mechanical guarding for turbine components, controlled pneumatic testing, noise exposure limits, and a workplace emergency evacuation plan with trained first-aid and fire wardens.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake; secure online filing and registration portal is myIR. Company formation and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) are administered by the New Zealand Companies Office within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register NZ_LTD as a New Zealand limited liability company at the New Zealand Companies Office under the Companies Act 1993; the Companies Office will issue the NZBN. Step 2: Using the NZBN, create a myIR login and submit the IRD number application for a New Zealand company or, where the controlling shareholder is offshore, the non-resident company registration path, providing the certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director and shareholder details, and each non-resident controlling party's overseas tax identification number. Step 3: Appoint a New Zealand resident agent for service of notices if IRD requires one for a non-resident-owned or offshore-managed company. Step 4: IRD issues the IRD number, which is the single statutory Tax Identification Number for income tax, GST, PAYE and other tax obligations; GST registration is applied for through myIR and the GST registration identifier is the same IRD number rather than a separate VAT ID. Step 5: Maintain current registration details in myIR and file all statutory tax returns through myIR or IRD-approved API-connected tax software.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election or a general hybrid entity classification election. A closely held New Zealand company with five or fewer owners may elect look-through company (LTC) treatment under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, making the company tax-transparent for New Zealand income tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch rules under subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 continue to apply to cross-border structures, and non-resident investors should obtain New Zealand tax advice before electing LTC status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; registration is compulsory once this threshold is exceeded, and voluntary registration is available to a supplier carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand. Non-resident suppliers of remote services and electronic marketplaces must register if their supplies to New Zealand consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or anti-fraud digital stamping requirement. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the Peppol network. GST returns must be filed electronically using myIR or IRD-approved API-integrated software. All GST invoices must contain the information required by section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including the supplier's GST/IRD number, invoice date, supplier and recipient details, description and quantity of goods, GST-exclusive amount, GST amount, and total payable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11(1)(a) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, a supply of goods is zero-rated where the supplier, or an agent on the supplier's behalf, exports the goods from New Zealand within 28 days after the time of supply. For ICU mechanical ventilators, zero-rating applies to the physical goods sold by NZ_LTD when the goods are removed from New Zealand to a destination outside New Zealand. Supporting services supplied directly in connection with the export may also be zero-rated under section 11(2) if the statutory conditions are satisfied. New Zealand has no exchange-control or FIRC-based condition for zero-rating, but the exporter must retain sufficient documentary evidence to demonstrate the physical export and the receipt of consideration from the non-resident purchaser. All records must be kept for seven years under section 51 of the Tax Administration Act 1994.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export declaration (Export Entry) lodged via the Trade Single Window, with customs-approved departure status for the ICU ventilators
Commercial invoice and packing list for the ICU ventilators cross-referenced to the Export Entry
Negotiable bill of lading or air waybill evidencing physical departure of the goods from New Zealand to the foreign purchaser

Bank inward remittance advice or foreign exchange conversion record, being the New Zealand banking equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate, showing export proceeds credited to NZ_LTD's New Zealand bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where the section 11 export conditions are not met within 28 days of supply, the supply becomes standard-rated and 15% GST is payable, together with use-of-money interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994. IRD may reassess prior GST returns and claw back input tax credits previously claimed in reliance on an invalid zero-rating position. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 can apply: 20% for failing to take reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Knowingly providing false or misleading export documents may also lead to criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994 or the Customs and Excise Act 2018 for inaccurate export declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ), exercising prudential supervision over registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989; the RBNZ administers no foreign exchange licensing, registration, or approval regime and is not a counterparty to cross-border payment authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar is fully convertible. New Zealand has accepted Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement, imposing no exchange controls, no capital account authorization requirements, and no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayment, or royalty and fee payments to non-resident shareholders. Non-residents may freely hold New Zealand dollar and foreign currency accounts. The only substantive cross-border compliance gates arise from the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, enforced by the Financial Markets Authority and the Police Financial Intelligence Unit, and from bank-level customer due diligence policies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratios, no repatriation deadlines, and no designated settlement currency for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in onshore or offshore foreign currency accounts. The only applicable disciplines are commercial (documentary compliance under UCP600 for letters of credit) and bank-driven (screening and monitoring of trade receipts within the customer risk profile).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational NZD account with subordinate foreign currency accounts; separate Capital Escrow Account required for ring-fenced subscription proceeds
Operational NZD account for clearing and supplier disbursements
Operational NZD account plus Government Letter of Credit advising, confirmation, and negotiation desk
Operational NZD account with trade finance and cross-currency hedging capacity
Operational NZD account limited to domestic clearing support

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium viability limited to operational payment routing and low-value supplier disbursements, with strict legal constraints. Offshore digital EMI providers hold no New Zealand banking registration under RBNZ supervision, cannot receive capital subscriptions in a manner satisfying escrow transparency, and cannot advise or negotiate documentary credits against New Zealand government procurement. Only EMIs registered under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and recognized as reporting entities under the AML/CFT Act may process incidental cross-border supplier wires; they are excluded from the capital escrow structure and from Government Letter of Credit settlement rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is not a statutory mandate; the AML/CFT Act requires identity verification to a reasonable standard. Major banks accept certified copies of passports, proof of residential address, Companies Office registry extracts, and a controlled video conference interview. In practice, for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced statutory-licensed medical device manufacturer with government procurement counterparties, the banks require at least one director with signing authority to complete an enhanced due diligence interview (in person or on a bank-approved secure video platform), and require the appointed New Zealand resident director to attest to beneficial ownership and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership or nominee shareholder layers failing the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) disclosure assessment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation from the New Zealand Companies Office; current register of directors and shareholders; a UBO declaration table identifying every natural person holding 25% or more; notarized declarations confirming absence of nominee arrangements; and an organizational chart tracing the full ownership chain to natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory-licensed medical device manufacturing activity flagged as Medium_Risk_Enhanced under sector-based bank policy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid statutory licence for the manufacture and supply of ICU mechanical ventilators under the Medicines Act 1981 and the Medical Devices Regulations 2014; ISO 13485 quality management system certificate covering the manufacturing site; and evidence of medical device registration with the applicable notified body or competent authority for each target export market.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an offshore parent or trust creating source-of-funds doubt
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved capital contribution resolutions; audited financial statements of the subscribing shareholder; a source-of-funds trail evidencing the ultimate origin of each wire; executed subscription agreements; and a sworn director declaration confirming the absence of third-party lending, crypto-conversion opacity, or unlawful provenance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment profile dominated by cross-border Government Letter of Credit and SWIFT wires inconsistent with stated revenue size
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed government procurement contracts or binding letters of intent with Crown procurement agencies; purchase order history; a 12-month treasury cash-flow projection aligning letter of credit maturities with inbound wires; and evidence that underlying shipments are supported by standard export documentation under defined Incoterms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse media flags on export-market distributors or end-customers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening clearances from a recognized screening provider; completed counterparty due diligence questionnaires for every distributor; a compliance attestation letter addressing end-use and end-user controls; and a restricted-party screening log demonstrating that all letter of credit applicants and beneficiaries passed the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists and New Zealand autonomous sanctions measures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscription wires execute over SWIFT MT103 through the correspondent clearing chain into the NZD operational or escrow account maintained with the selected registered bank, with final settlement across the RBNZ Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). The remitter must include a purpose description referencing direct investment and use the OECD/IMF Balance of Payments classification for direct investment equity capital. The receiving bank requires the underlying subscription agreement, board resolution, and UBO declaration prior to crediting; no RBNZ approval or foreign exchange filing is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for component procurement and tolling services route over SWIFT MT103 priority wires for supplier payments and via documentary letters of credit for larger component shipments under UCP600, with advising and negotiation through the bank's trade finance desk. Government procurement sales are settled by Government Letter of Credit instruments issued by Crown procurement agents, advised and negotiated in NZD or USD through the major bank's documentary credit team. All outbound payments are subject exclusively to bank-level sanctions screening and AML/CFT customer due diligence, with no central bank approval or exchange control permit requirement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Dual-currency deliverable forward contracts quoted by the tier 1 bank for NZD/USD and NZD/EUR, with tenors matched to government contract payment milestones and letter of credit maturities

Outright deliverable foreign exchange forwards (NDFs are not needed for the NZD market given full convertibility and an active deliverable forward market; NDFs are considered only for illiquid cross-currency pairs not otherwise deliverable in New Zealand)
Foreign exchange swaps executed for timing conversion between USD receipts and NZD operating cash requirements
Cross-currency swaps for medium-term hedging of USD-denominated capital or refinancing exposures beyond twelve months, subject to the bank's ISDA and supporting collateral agreement framework

Vanilla FX options on the deliverable NZD market, including call and put structures, permitted under the bank's standard derivative execution policy upon documented board-approved treasury hedging policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the company (Companies Act 1993, ss 211–213)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment – MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: the Annual Return must be filed during the company's 'return month' (the month of incorporation anniversary) and is due no later than the last day of that month (the return date); the Registrar issues an e-reminder at the opening of the return month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Annual Return filing fee has been abolished, but non-filing places the company in default; the Registrar issues a formal late notice and, if no return is lodged, may strike the company off the New Zealand Companies Register (removal or deregistration) in accordance with Companies Act 1993 s 318, which dissolves the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) confirmation (Companies (Beneficial Ownership Disclosure) Amendment Act 2024)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The BOR confirmation is filed together with the Annual Return and is certified as accurate as at the return date; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the BOR within 10 working days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to establish, update, or annually confirm the BOR is a statutory infringement offence exposing the company to a fine of up to NZ$50,000 (approx. USD 30,500); continued default may additionally ground deregistration from the Companies Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory for (i) 'large' NZ companies that meet at least 2 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013 s 45 tests — total assets above NZ$60 million, total revenue above NZ$30 million, or 50 or more full-time-equivalent employees; (ii) FMC reporting entities that have made public offers of equity or debt; and (iii) any company where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares validly require the board to appoint an auditor under Companies Act 1993 s 199. Private Ltds below these thresholds are audit-exempt but remain obliged to prepare financial statements in accordance with applicable XRB standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB): NZ equivalents of IFRS (NZ IFRS) for large and FMC reporting entities; NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2) for medium for-profit entities; and the XRB simplified reporting framework (small companies) based on IFRS for SMEs. Financial statements must be prepared as at balance date and, for 'large' companies, filed with the Companies Office.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Disclosure) Amendment Act 2024, the NZ Ltd must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office recording individuals with 25% or more of the issued shares or voting rights, or with significant influence or control over the company. Each share allotment or transfer that alters beneficial ownership must be entered in the BOR within 10 working days, and a director must confirm the BOR as true and complete in the course of filing the Annual Return each year. Knowingly submitting false BOR information constitutes a separate director offence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register) — Companies Act 1993 s 88
Register of Directors — Companies Act 1993 s 289
Minute Book (records of shareholder meetings, board meetings, and written resolutions) — Companies Act 1993 s 189
Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) — Companies (Beneficial Ownership Disclosure) Amendment Act 2024

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–900 per annum (approx NZ$400–1,500): typical market range for a registered office address plus NZ chartered corporate secretarial and annual return agency services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–25,000 per annum (approx NZ$8,000–40,000): typical independent audit fee range for a small-to-mid-size NZ private manufacturing company; the exact fee scales with turnover, audit procedures over ventilator inventory and export receivables, and the statutory trigger (large-company test or shareholder requisition).
